samples.summary: Overlay guard is a hard-coded Radix selector whitelist; Escape-dismissing overlays that don't carry `data-state="open"` bypass it and get both dismissed and navigated away from
samples.evidence: The new guard only recognises layers matching `[role="dialog"][data-state="open"]` etc. (image-viewer.tsx:22-38). The repo already contains hand-rolled, Escape-dismissed overlays that render `role="dialog"` with NO `data-state` attribute — `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/DocsCommentPopover.tsx:80`, `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:618`, `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/components/comments/CommentPopover.tsx:83` — and a `role="listbox"` mention menu without `data-state` at `packages/frontend/src/components/comments/components/CommentComposer.tsx:281`. I checked every overlay reachable on the `/f/:id` image route today (share-dialog.tsx:155 Radix Dialog, notification-bell.tsx:46 Radix Popover, ui/sheet.tsx Radix Dialog for the mobile sidebar, app-sidebar's create-workspace Dialog, ui/select.tsx popper Select) and all of them do match the selector, so I could not confirm a live bypass — hence low confidence. The fragility lives on the new code: the guard would be robust if it keyed off whether the keydown target/`document.activeElement` is inside the viewer subtree (or off a shell-owned "layer open" context) rather than off a fixed list of Radix markup shapes.
searchedFor: read ui/dialog.tsx, ui/sheet.tsx, ui/popover.tsx, ui/select.tsx, ui/tooltip.tsx

samples.summary: Window keydown listener moved from bubble to capture phase, so any child handler that used `stopPropagation` to suppress viewer navigation no longer can
samples.evidence: `window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey, true)` (image-viewer.tsx:163) now runs before every bubble-phase handler in the tree. The repo relies on bubble-phase `stopPropagation` to shield window-level key handlers elsewhere (e.g. `packages/frontend/src/components/table-grid-picker.tsx:69` and `packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-view.tsx:662-669`, which documents exactly that technique). Nothing currently on the `/f/:id` image route uses it (I checked every `stopPropagation` in packages/frontend/src), so this is a latent trap rather than a live break: future in-viewer key-consuming UI will silently fail to suppress prev/next/Esc.

samples.summary: Back/Esc navigation pushes a history entry while the sibling not-found redirect replaces, so history behaviour differs between the two consumers of the same path
samples.evidence: `ImageFileLayout` uses `navigate(documentsPath)` (file-detail.tsx:131-134), while `FileShell`'s redirect uses `navigate(documentsPath, { replace: true })` (packages/frontend/src/app/files/file-shell.tsx:67). After clicking the new back button the browser Back button returns to the image, so repeated back/Esc use grows the stack — a consumer-visible inconsistency for a control shaped like "go back", not a functional break.

samples.summary: `useDocumentsPath` returns `/documents` until the shared `["workspaces"]` query resolves, so an early Esc/back click lands on the wrong list
samples.evidence: The hook has no loading signal: with `workspaces` still empty it yields `/documents` (use-documents-path.ts:18-21). `file-detail.tsx:128` builds `close` from it and hands that closure to both the header button and `ImageViewer`'s Esc path, so a keystroke during the first paint navigates to the workspace-less list instead of `/w/:slug`. `FileShell`'s redirect (file-shell.tsx:64-69) had the same race before this change, so this is pre-existing behaviour newly exposed on two more interactive entry points.

searchedFor: read ui/dialog.tsx, ui/sheet.tsx, ui/popover.tsx, ui/select.tsx, ui/tooltip.tsx

verdict.reason: The guard and the cited no-`data-state` overlays all exist as described, but none of the claimed bypassing sites is reachable while the viewer's keydown handler is mounted, so there is no blast-radius defect. `ImageViewer` mounts only at file-detail.tsx:152 (the `/f/:id` `type === "image"` branch inside `FileShell`) and shared-document.tsx:766 (share link, no `onClose`, prev/next disabled by `enabled: !token` at image-viewer.tsx:100/116). The four overlays lacking `data-state` render only inside docs-view.tsx:599 / docs-view.tsx:616 and sheet-view.tsx:1670 — route-exclusive views that never co-mount with `ImageViewer`. The image route's own shell (file-shell.tsx:108-131) contributes only Radix layers that do match the selector, and its one hand-rolled Escape handler is the title `<input>` at site-header.tsx:64-70, already excluded by the INPUT/TEXTAREA/contentEditable early return at image-viewer.tsx:149-156; the mention listbox at CommentComposer.tsx:281 is likewise only open while a `<textarea>` is focused (CommentComposer.tsx:255-279), so it too hits that early return. The reviewer concedes no live bypass and states the real concern is that "the fragility lives on the new code" — a robustness/design critique of the selector list inside the diff, stateable without leaving the diff, which this lens explicitly defers to the correctness/design-fit lenses. No reachable bypass, no broken external consumer, no changed contract left unupdated.

finding.summary: New `hasOpenOverlay()` guard is tripped by the sidebar's *invisible* nav tooltips, silently killing Esc/arrow keys in the image viewer
finding.evidence: `hasOpenOverlay()` (packages/frontend/src/app/files/image-viewer.tsx:32-34) matches `[data-radix-popper-content-wrapper]`. `SidebarMenuButton` wraps every nav item in a Radix `Tooltip` and renders `TooltipContent` with only `hidden={state !== "collapsed" || isMobile}` (packages/frontend/src/components/ui/sidebar.tsx:534-543); `TooltipContent` is portaled (packages/frontend/src/components/ui/tooltip.tsx:38-51) and `TooltipProvider` uses `delayDuration = 0`. `nav-main.tsx:44` passes `tooltip={item.title}` for Documents / Data Sources / Settings, which `FileShell` mounts for the image layout (file-shell.tsx:110). So merely hovering — or keyboard-focusing, since Radix Tooltip opens on focus and stays open while focused — a sidebar nav item mounts a popper wrapper even when the tooltip is visually `hidden` on an expanded desktop sidebar. From that instant `hasOpenOverlay()` returns true and both Esc (back to the list) and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (prev/next image) do nothing, with no overlay on screen to explain it. The fix belongs on the new code: the guard should scope to genuinely dismissable, visible layers (e.g. require `data-state="open"` on the wrapper's content and exclude `role="tooltip"`/`[hidden]`), not any mounted popper.

verdict.reason: The finding's core evidence is not present. It claims `hasOpenOverlay()` matches bare `[data-radix-popper-content-wrapper]`, but the actual selector at packages/frontend/src/app/files/image-viewer.tsx:37 is `[data-radix-popper-content-wrapper] > [data-state="open"]:not([data-slot="tooltip-content"])` — it keys off the content element, requires `data-state="open"` (Radix tooltips report `instant-open`/`delayed-open`, never `open`), and explicitly excludes tooltip content. `TooltipContent` sets `data-slot="tooltip-content"` at packages/frontend/src/components/ui/tooltip.tsx:40, so the sidebar nav tooltips at packages/frontend/src/components/ui/sidebar.tsx:534-543 cannot trip the guard. Lines 32-34 the finding cites as the selector are actually the comment explaining why the wrapper is deliberately not matched, describing this exact sidebar scenario. The remediation the finding prescribes is already implemented, and a regression test at packages/frontend/src/app/files/__tests__/image-viewer.test.tsx:131-139 mounts a nav tooltip, asserts the popper wrapper exists, and asserts Esc still invokes onClose.
